title: Positive iteration and coefficient descent of a semilinear germ square
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a chosen algebraic closure $\Qlb$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Let $Y_0$ be proper of finite type over $k_0$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $a_Y:Y\to s$. Put $\gamma=(c\mapsto c^q)^{-1}$, $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ and $g=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times h$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. On the derived-complete integral constructible categories [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], write $A=La_Y^*$, $R=Ra_{Y*}$, $P=Lg^*$, $Q=Lh^*$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Use the specified associative pullback-composition comparisons [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], represented on the simultaneous whole coefficient systems [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. For $M\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, let $\varepsilon:AR\to\mathrm{id}$ be the ordinary adjunction counit [fix-prop-adjunctions], and let $\mathcal E_M=\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M):QRM\to RPM$ be the actual strict-system mate followed by derived inverse limit of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange](1). For a $k$-point $x:s\to Y$ put $Z_x=Lx^*$, $x_j=g^jxh^{-j}$, and let $u_x:Z_xA\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ and $b_{1,x,M}:QZ_{x_1}M\xrightarrow{\sim}Z_xPM$ be the specified comparisons for $a_Yx=\mathrm{id}_s$ and $gx=x_1h$. Define $v_x^M=Z_x(\varepsilon_M)u_x(RM)^{-1}:RM\to Z_xM$.

For every finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Qlb$, assume the one-step identity
$$v_x^{PM}\mathcal E_M=b_{1,x,M}Q(v_{x_1}^M)$$
for all integral $M$ and $k$-points $x$. Put $V=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], let $\iota:V\to VQ$ be the specified restriction--insertion--pullback point transport [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], $e_x^M=V(v_x^M)$ and $\tau_M=V(\mathcal E_M)\iota_{RM}$ [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. For $r\ge1$ put $S_r=P^r$, $J_r=Q^r$, with $S_{r+1}=PS_r$, $J_{r+1}=QJ_r$, and define
$$\widehat\tau_{1,M}=\tau_M,\qquad\widehat\tau_{r+1,M}=\tau_{S_rM}\widehat\tau_{r,M},$$
$$\widehat I_{1,N}=\iota_N,\qquad\widehat I_{r+1,N}=\iota_{J_rN}\widehat I_{r,N},$$
$$\widehat b_{1,x,M}=b_{1,x,M},\qquad\widehat b_{r+1,x,M}=b_{1,x,S_rM}Q(\widehat b_{r,x_1,M}).$$
Let $P_r=L(g^r)^*$, $Q_r=L(h^r)^*$, let $d_r:P_r\xrightarrow{\sim}S_r$ and $f_r:Q_r\xrightarrow{\sim}J_r$ be the specified iterated comparisons, and let $b_{r,x,M}:Q_rZ_{x_r}M\xrightarrow{\sim}Z_xP_rM$ be the comparison for $g^rx=x_rh^r$. Put $\tau_M^{[r]}=VR(d_{r,M}^{-1})\widehat\tau_{r,M}$ and $I_N^{[r]}=V(f_{r,N}^{-1})\widehat I_{r,N}$. Then, naturally in integral $M$, one has
$$e_x^{PM}\tau_M=V(b_{1,x,M})\iota_{Z_{x_1}M}e_{x_1}^M,$$
$$e_x^{S_rM}\widehat\tau_{r,M}=V(\widehat b_{r,x,M})\widehat I_{r,Z_{x_r}M}e_{x_r}^M,$$
$$Z_x(d_{r,M}^{-1})\widehat b_{r,x,M}=b_{r,x,M}f_{r,Z_{x_r}M}^{-1},$$
and consequently
$$e_x^{P_rM}\tau_M^{[r]}=V(b_{r,x,M})I_{Z_{x_r}M}^{[r]}e_{x_r}^M.$$
Use raw scalar localization for $D^b_c(Y,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and common finite stages for $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], with the operations and comparisons transported by [lem-fix-operation-reduction] and point transport by [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2). Every displayed equality remains valid with these specified factors for $\Lambda=E$ and $\Lambda=\Qlb$, naturally in every morphism at those coefficient stages. In particular the rational germs are the scalar-localization images of the integral $v_x$ followed by $V$, and the $\Qlb$ arrows are the common-stage classes of the corresponding finite-field arrows; the identities commute with further finite coefficient extension. No Weil structure or finite-Tor hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text:
First record the naturalities used below. For an integral morphism $t:M\to M'$, naturality of the adjunction counit and of $u_x$ gives
$$Z_x(t)v_x^M=v_x^{M'}R(t),\qquad VZ_x(t)e_x^M=e_x^{M'}VR(t).$$
Indeed substitute $v_x^M=Z_x(\varepsilon_M)u_x(RM)^{-1}$, move $Z_xAR(t)$ across $Z_x(\varepsilon)$ by counit naturality, and then use $Z_xAR(t)u_x(RM)^{-1}=u_x(RM')^{-1}R(t)$. The counit is the ordinary one in [fix-prop-adjunctions](1); the comparisons are natural by [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition]. The maps $b_{1,x}$ and $b_{r,x}$ are natural for the same reason, and $\tau$ is natural by [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. The given $g,h$ are scheme automorphisms, not asserted to be $k$-linear. Since $a_Yg=ha_Y$, one has $a_Yx_j=h^j(a_Yx)h^{-j}=\mathrm{id}$ and $gx_j=x_{j+1}h$ by cancellation. Thus every moving point used in the induction is a $k$-point.

proof.text:
Apply the functor $V$ to the assumed one-step identity and precompose with $\iota_{RM}$. Naturality [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2), applied to the actual derived morphism $v_{x_1}^M:RM\to Z_{x_1}M$, says
$$VQ(v_{x_1}^M)\iota_{RM}=\iota_{Z_{x_1}M}V(v_{x_1}^M).$$
Consequently
$$e_x^{PM}\tau_M=V(v_x^{PM}\mathcal E_M)\iota_{RM}=V(b_{1,x,M})\iota_{Z_{x_1}M}e_{x_1}^M.$$
This proves the first displayed conclusion and the uncontracted formula at $r=1$. It uses the specified $\mathcal E$ only through the hypothesis; no replacement of its strict-system mate is made.

proof.text:
Induct simultaneously for all $k$-points $x$ on $r\ge1$. The base is step 2. Suppose the uncontracted formula holds at $r$ for every point, and put $N=Z_{x_{r+1}}M$. Step 2 for the object $S_rM$, followed by the inductive hypothesis at $x_1$, gives
$$e_x^{S_{r+1}M}\widehat\tau_{r+1,M}=V(b_{1,x,S_rM})\iota_{Z_{x_1}S_rM}V(\widehat b_{r,x_1,M})\widehat I_{r,N}e_{x_{r+1}}^M.$$
Here the $r$-th moving point starting from $x_1$ is $x_{r+1}$, by step 1. Apply naturality of $\iota$ to $\widehat b_{r,x_1,M}:J_rN\to Z_{x_1}S_rM$ to replace the middle pair by
$$\iota_{Z_{x_1}S_rM}V(\widehat b_{r,x_1,M})=VQ(\widehat b_{r,x_1,M})\iota_{J_rN}.$$
Functoriality of $V$ and the two defining recurrences now give exactly $V(\widehat b_{r+1,x,M})\widehat I_{r+1,N}e_{x_{r+1}}^M$. This proves the uncontracted equality at every positive integer.

proof.text:
Write $F_f=Lf^*$ and $c_{f,t}:F_{tf}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_fF_t$ for the specified composition maps. The comparison associated to $g^rx=x_rh^r$ is
$$b_{r,x}=c_{x,g^r}\,c_{h^r,x_r}^{-1}.$$
The common source of these two composition maps is identified using that equality of scheme maps. Put $C_r=c_{g,g^r}:P_{r+1}\to PP_r$ and $H_r=c_{h,h^r}:Q_{r+1}\to QQ_r$. The associativity equation of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], with the equality-compatible whole-system normalization of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], gives
$$Z_x(C_{r,M})b_{r+1,x,M}=b_{1,x,P_rM}\,Q(b_{r,x_1,M})\,H_{r,Z_{x_{r+1}}M}.$$
To check the equation, expand each $b$ by the preceding formula. Apply associativity to the three composable maps $(x,g,g^r)$, $(h,x_1,g^r)$ and $(h,h^r,x_{r+1})$, and cancel the inverse composition factors between successive applications. The two shared intermediate scheme maps are $gx=x_1h$ and $g^rx_1=x_{r+1}h^r$; their composite is $g^{r+1}x=x_{r+1}h^{r+1}$. Thus the resulting outer factors are precisely the left side. These are equalities of the specified realized comparisons, not an inference from equality of individual finite reductions.

proof.text:
The iterated comparisons satisfy $d_1=f_1=\mathrm{id}$ and
$$d_{r+1}=P(d_r)C_r,\qquad f_{r+1}=Q(f_r)H_r.$$
Induct to prove the equivalent contraction equation
$$Z_x(d_{r,M})b_{r,x,M}=\widehat b_{r,x,M}f_{r,Z_{x_r}M}.$$
The base is the unit normalization. For the step, substitute step 4 and move $Z_xP(d_{r,M})$ across $b_{1,x,P_rM}$ by its naturality. The left side becomes
$$b_{1,x,S_rM}\,Q\bigl(Z_{x_1}(d_{r,M})b_{r,x_1,M}\bigr)\,H_{r,Z_{x_{r+1}}M}.$$
Apply the inductive contraction equation at $x_1$ and combine $Q(f_r)H_r=f_{r+1}$. This is $\widehat b_{r+1,x,M}f_{r+1,Z_{x_{r+1}}M}$ by definition. Associativity and unitality here are those of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Postcompose with $f_r^{-1}$ and precompose on the target with $Z_x(d_r^{-1})$ to obtain the third displayed conclusion.

proof.text:
Apply the naturality of $e_x$ from step 1 to $d_{r,M}^{-1}:S_rM\to P_rM$, and then use steps 3 and 5. With $N=Z_{x_r}M$, this gives
$$\begin{aligned}e_x^{P_rM}\tau_M^{[r]}&=VZ_x(d_{r,M}^{-1})e_x^{S_rM}\widehat\tau_{r,M}\\&=V\bigl(Z_x(d_{r,M}^{-1})\widehat b_{r,x,M}\bigr)\widehat I_{r,N}e_{x_r}^M\\&=V(b_{r,x,M})V(f_{r,N}^{-1})\widehat I_{r,N}e_{x_r}^M\\&=V(b_{r,x,M})I_N^{[r]}e_{x_r}^M.\end{aligned}$$
This is the contracted integral equality. All factors in steps 2--6 are composites, functor images or components of natural transformations from step 1 and [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2); induction therefore gives their naturality in every integral derived morphism. The computations never require a Weil isomorphism $PM\cong M$ or finite Tor-amplitude of a reduction.

proof.text: Pass first to $E$. In the raw scalar localization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], objects are the integral objects and a morphism is a finite sum $\sum_i t_i\otimes a_i$. The operation comparisons and the adjunction counit are the prescribed rationalizations by [lem-fix-operation-reduction]; the point fiber acts by $t\otimes a\mapsto a(V(t)\otimes E)$ by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point](3); the rational point transport is by definition $\iota^E_N=\iota^{\mathcal O_E}_N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], and the rational exchange $\mathcal E$ is by definition the scalar-localization image of the integral $\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}$ [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange](1); the specified $\iota$ is natural at this stage by [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2). Hence the rational germ is the image of $Z_x(\varepsilon_M)u_x(RM)^{-1}$ under scalar localization, followed by the rational $V$. Apply the localization functor, and then the rational point-fiber functor where appropriate, to the equalities of steps 2--6. They preserve composition and inverses of the displayed isomorphisms, giving all four equalities with precisely their stated factors over $E$. Naturality holds for each $t_i$ by the integral proof; multiplying that equation by $a_i$ and adding proves it for every localized morphism. No claim that $M$ has a new integral lattice is needed: localization has the same objects.

proof.text:
For $E\subset L$, [lem-fix-operation-reduction] identifies scalar extension of the operations, counit and exchange with their specified versions over $L$, while [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] identifies all finite composites of pullback comparisons. The point-fiber comparison is the natural isomorphism of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], with its identity and successive-extension equations; [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2) gives compatibility of $\iota$ under these same comparisons. Thus substituting into each definition of $v,e,\tau,d,f,b,\widehat\tau,\widehat I,\widehat b$ shows that every factor over $E$, after extension and those conjugations, is the corresponding factor over $L$. For the three recurrences this follows by induction: extension preserves their products and functor images, and the identity case starts the induction. Consequently the equalities of step 7 are preserved by further finite extension.

Over $\Qlb$ the point transport and the exchange are, by definition, the classes represented at a finite stage $E'$ by $\iota^{E'}$ [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] and by $\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*,E'}$ [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange](1). Now [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] represents every morphism, and each finite diagram here for fixed $r$, at one common finite field $L$. Form all the factors and the naturality squares at that $L$ and apply step 7. Their equalities therefore give equalities of common-stage classes. Two representatives agree after a further common extension; the compatibility just proved preserves the equations there, so the result is independent of the representatives and natural for every common-stage morphism. This proves the asserted $\Qlb$ identities and their coefficient-extension compatibility.
